title: A typical day
paragraphs: My name is Aizhan and I am a first-year student at WKU. Every day at university is busy, but I love my routine. My alarm rings at 6:30 every morning. I get up immediately — I never press snooze! I wash my face, brush my teeth, and make my bed. Then I check my phone for messages from my family. By 7:00, I am ready to start the day.

I go to the cafeteria for breakfast at 7:15. I usually eat porridge or an omelette with bread and a glass of orange juice. Sometimes I have a banana or an apple too. Dias always arrives at the cafeteria at 7:20 and we sit together. He always orders tea and toast. We talk about our plans for the day and check our timetables before classes begin.

Our classes start at 8:30 every morning. I walk from the dormitory to the main academic building — it takes about ten minutes. I like this short walk because I listen to English podcasts on my earphones. When I arrive at the classroom, I take out my notebook and pen and prepare for the lesson. I always sit in the second row — it helps me concentrate.

In the morning, we usually have two or three subjects. On Mondays and Wednesdays, my first lesson is English with Ms. Aigerim. I love English lessons — we speak, read, write, and listen. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, I have Mathematics first. Mathematics is my most difficult subject, but I study hard and ask Ms. Aigerim for help after class.

At 12:00, we have a one-hour lunch break. I go to the cafeteria with Dias and our classmates. We usually eat soup, a main course, and compote — a traditional Kazakh fruit drink. After lunch, Dias and I often sit in the library for twenty minutes. I review my morning notes and Dias checks his homework. Then we go back to class at 1:00.

In the afternoon, we have two more subjects. On most days, I have Computer Science and History of Kazakhstan. I love Computer Science — we learn to write programs and work with data. History of Kazakhstan is also interesting because I learn about my country's culture and traditions. Classes finish at 3:30 pm every day.

After classes, I go back to my room and rest for thirty minutes. Then I start my homework and revision. I study for about two hours — usually from 4:30 to 6:30. I do my English exercises first, then Mathematics, and then other subjects. At 7:00, I go to dinner. After dinner, I call my parents in Aktobe — we talk for about twenty minutes every evening.

I usually go to sleep at 10:30 pm. Before I sleep, I write in my diary for five minutes — I write about the best moment of my day. My favourite moment today? When Ms. Aigerim said my essay was excellent! I feel happy and motivated at WKU. Every day is different, but every day I learn something new. That is the best thing about university life!

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: Aizhan, what time do you get up every morning?

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: At 6:30! My alarm rings and I get up immediately. You?

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: I get up at 7:00... sometimes 7:10. I press snooze once or twice!

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: Ha! No wonder you always look tired at breakfast. Do you eat in the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: Yes, I have tea and toast. Simple but fast! What about you?

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: I eat porridge or an omelette. Breakfast is very important — I need energy!

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: True. Hey, what do you do after classes in the afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: I rest for thirty minutes, then I study from 4:30 to 6:30. Two hours.

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: Two hours every day? That's a lot! I usually study for one hour.

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: I know, but I want good grades. Do you call your parents every evening?

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: Yes, at about 8:00. My mum always asks about my food and my grades!

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: Same! Mine too. I go to sleep at 10:30. What time do you sleep?
